moves.headline: PDD Holdings rose 11% as profit beat expectations even though revenue did not grow
moves.summary: PDD’s third-quarter revenue was flat at RMB108.3 billion, but earnings came in about 12% above analyst estimates because the Temu owner cut sales and marketing spending by RMB5 billion. Investors had feared profit would fall.
why: PDD Holdings reported third-quarter results on November 19. Total revenues were RMB108.3 billion, about $16.2 billion, the same as a year earlier. Net income attributable to shareholders was RMB29.5 billion against RMB29.3 billion, and adjusted net income was RMB31.0 billion against RMB31.4 billion. Earnings per ADS were about 12% above the analyst consensus.

Profit held up because costs fell. Sales and marketing expenses dropped to RMB25.3 billion from RMB30.3 billion a year earlier, a cut of about 17%, while research and development spending rose. Operating profit was RMB31.2 billion. A company that had warned repeatedly that profitability would suffer during an investment phase instead held its earnings level.

The relief is in the gap between what was feared and what was reported. PDD’s management has spent a year telling investors to expect lower profits as it supports merchants and adapts its Temu business to tariffs and tighter rules on low-value parcels. Flat revenue with stable profit is a better outcome than that guidance implied.
context: The harder question is growth. A company that was growing revenue by more than 40% two years ago reported no growth at all this quarter, and management repeated that it remains in a ‘strategic investment phase’. The rally reflects a low starting valuation and low expectations more than a return to the earlier pace.
